`lsdev`: list the devices on the bus.

## Synopsis

<strong>lsdev</strong> \[<strong>-i</strong>\]

## Description

<strong>lsdev</strong> lists the devices on the computer's bus, as a table with a header row:

<strong>NAME</strong>
: The kernel's name for it: its type and its place among devices of that type in bus order (<strong>terminal0</strong>, <strong>storage1</strong>). A device with data to read or write (the EEPROM) has a file by that name in <em>/dev</em>.

<strong>TYPE</strong>
: What kind of device it is.

<strong>PATH</strong>
: Its slot address, as <strong>sata:0</strong> or <strong>exp:2</strong>; <strong>-</strong> for a device that is not in a slot (a cabled screen, a card in a hub).

<strong>ID</strong>
: Its id address, <strong>id:</strong><em>uuid</em><strong>,</strong> which names it however it is connected. Shown only with <strong>-i</strong>.

<strong>LABEL</strong>
: The name the player gave its item, if any.

Rows are in bus order. The list is the kernel's: it reads the bus when the bus says it changed (or a device it called is gone), so just after a change it may be a moment behind.

## Options

<strong>-i</strong>
: Add the <strong>ID</strong> column.

## Exit status

0 on success; 1 on any other argument.

## Notes

Bus positions (the numbers in the case view) are not addresses; programs name devices by their path or id.

## See also

<strong>ls</strong>(1), <strong>mount</strong>(1), <strong>df</strong>(1)
